newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- A contender for the post of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Chief Executive, Simon Li, refused to say where he had obtained confidential information about Hong Kong's transitional budget.
-- Guangzhou minicipality in China has raised the registration fee for possessing a dog to 10,000 yuan a year.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Unnamed sources said Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health has worsened.
-- The trial of Chinese dissident Wang Dan is to begin Wednesday. His mother would not reveal the name of Wang's lawyer for fear of affecting his future business.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- Beijing has demanded that Tokyo settles the Diaoyu islands issue.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company has prepared a draft for public consultation, allowing individual investors access to its services.
-- Beijing-funded HONG KONG COMMERCIAL DAILY -- The Hong Kong government planned to rent or sell 13 government apartments, which would bring in more than HK$200 million.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST --Beijing has reportedly set up a reserve fund to ensure the stability of the stock market after the handover.
-- Beijing is studying a plan to inject at least 2 million yuan into China Lucky Film, the country's biggest photographic film maker, which is threathened by competitors Fuji and Kodak.
-- Revived confidence has brought HK$29 billion worth of major property transactions in the first nine months of 1996.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong turned in weaker-than-expected trade performance in September as deficit rose 6.23 per cent to HK$4.6 billion year-on-year.
